extra.message: SQL injection in SQLinjection.run(): the 'id' query parameter (handler.params['id'][0]) is concatenated directly into the SQL string "SELECT id, username, firstname, lastname, email, session FROM users WHERE id=" + id and passed to cursor.execute(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (UNION-based extraction of all users including passwords/sessions, etc.). The sqlite error is also returned to the caller (line 41), enabling error-based injection.

SQL injection in AuthBypass.run() login check: the 'password' parameter is concatenated unsanitized into "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='" + username + "' AND password='" + password + "'". Only 'username' is filtered with re.sub(r"[^\w]", '', ...) at line 282; 'password' is used raw, so a classic ' OR '1'='1 payload bypasses authentication entirely (CWE-287/CWE-89). The resulting sqlite error is reflected into the response at line 291, aiding error-based exploitation.

Remote command execution in do_BDR(): when risk >= 3, the raw HTTP request path (self.path[1:]) is passed to subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True). Any client can send a request like 'BDR /id HTTP/1.1' (or embed shell metacharacters) and execute arbitrary OS commands on the server, with output returned in the response.

Command injection in CommandInjection.run(): the 'domain' query parameter is concatenated into ' '.join([command, domain]) and executed via subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True) at risk level 3. A payload such as 'www.google.com;id' executes arbitrary shell commands.

Insecure deserialization in UnsafeDeserialization.run(): user-supplied 'object' parameter is base64-decoded and passed directly to pickle.loads() at risk level 3. Deserializing attacker-controlled pickle data yields arbitrary code execution (the class itself ships an RCE gadget with __reduce__ calling os.system at lines 178-181).

Path traversal in PathTraversal.run(): the 'path' query parameter is used directly in open(os.path.abspath(path), 'rb') with no validation or directory restriction. Requests like /docs?path=../../etc/passwd or /docs?path=ssl/key.pem read arbitrary files from the server filesystem.

Path traversal in StaticHandler.find(): the raw request path is concatenated into open('./{}'.format(path)) without normalization or confinement to a web root. The request path is never URL-decoded or sanitized in do_GET (line 198 only strips the query string), so 'GET /../ssl/key.pem' or '/../db/users.xml' reads files outside the intended static directory.

Server-side request forgery in PathTraversal.run(): when the user-controlled 'path' parameter contains '://', it is passed to urllib.request.urlopen(path), letting an attacker make the server fetch arbitrary URLs (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ or internal services) and read the response.

Reflected XSS in XSSReflected.run(): the 'msg' query parameter is taken from handler.params and returned unescaped as page content; TemplateHandler.get_content() inserts it verbatim into the HTML template. A request like /post?msg=<script>alert(1)</script> executes script in the victim's browser. The server also explicitly sends 'X-XSS-Protection: 0' (handlers.py line 237).

Stored XSS in XSSStored.run(): guestbook comments submitted via the 'comment' parameter are persisted (parameterized INSERT at line 88) but rendered back without escaping via '{}'.format(column) at line 97. A stored

Second-order stored XSS in XSRequestForgery.run(): the user's email (attacker-controllable via the CSRF-able /settings?email= endpoint at lines 322-325, with no input validation) is inserted unescaped into the HTML form via value="{}" at line 341 and .format(user[2], user[3], user[4]) at line 347. An attribute-breaking payload such as '"><script>...' executes when the settings page is viewed.

Stored XSS in SessionHijacking.run(): database user fields (including the email column that is attacker-modifiable through /settings?email=) are interpolated unescaped into HTML at lines 256-261. A malicious email value containing markup executes when the /profile page is rendered.

Open redirect in UnvalidatedRedirect.run(): the 'path' query parameter is inserted unvalidated into window.location.replace('{path}') in a script block, redirecting victims to arbitrary external sites (phishing). Because the value lands inside a JavaScript string literal, it also allows script-context injection (e.g. ');alert(1);//).

extra.message: Open redirect in SessionFixation.run(): the user-controlled 'path' parameter is embedded unvalidated into window.location = '{path}' in a JavaScript block, enabling redirection to arbitrary external sites and JS string-context injection.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: Session fixation in SessionFixation.run(): the server accepts a session ID supplied via the 'session' URL parameter and sets it as the SESSIONID cookie (cookie['SESSIONID'] = session). Combined with the login flow (handlers.py lines 199-203 only mint a new token when no cookie is present), an attacker can force a known session ID onto a victim and hijack the authenticated session after login.

Missing authorization / execution-after-redirect in ExecutionAfterRedirect.run(): the /admin page content ('Manage Users', 'Update Database Settings') is always included in the response; for unauthenticated requests the code merely appends a client-side JavaScript redirect to /login instead of enforcing access server-side. Any client that ignores the redirect (e.g. curl) receives the admin content without authentication.

cwe: CWE-602: Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security

extra.message: Cross-site request forgery in XSRequestForgery.run(): the authenticated user's email is changed via a simple GET request (/settings?email=...) based solely on the session cookie, with no CSRF token, no SameSite cookie attribute, and a state-changing action performed over GET. An attacker site can force a logged-in victim's browser to update the email (and chain into stored XSS).

Cross-site request forgery in Clickjacking.run(): the authenticated user's account is irreversibly deleted via a GET request (/danger?delete=1) with no CSRF token, no SameSite cookie protection, and no anti-clickjacking headers (no X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors in handlers.py lines 236-238). Any malicious page (e.g. or a hidden iframe) can delete a logged-in victim's account.

Hardcoded backdoor credentials in AuthBypass.run(): 'if username == 'dsvpwa' and password == 'dsvpwa'' grants a successful login to a fixed username/password pair compiled into the source code, bypassing the database credential check for anyone who knows the pair.

Session tokens are generated with random.sample(string.ascii_letters + string.digits, 20) using the non-cryptographic Mersenne Twister PRNG. Its internal state can be recovered from observed outputs, allowing session-ID prediction. The secrets module should be used for session identifiers.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak PRNG

extra.message: The SimpleCookie jar is a class attribute (VulnHTTPRequestHandler.cookie) shared by all requests and threads of the ThreadingHTTPServer. do_GET mutates it via self.cookie.load(...) (line 199) and later echoes every morsel back in Set-Cookie headers (lines 232-234), so concurrent requests race on one shared object: one user's SESSIONID can be overwritten with or leaked into another user's response.

cwe: CWE-488: Exposure of Data Element to Wrong Session

extra.message: Session cookies are emitted via morsel.OutputString() without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes. The missing HttpOnly flag lets any of the XSS vulnerabilities steal SESSIONID via document.cookie (session hijacking); missing Secure sends the cookie over plaintext HTTP; missing SameSite enables the CSRF attacks.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The server explicitly sends 'X-XSS-Protection: 0', disabling the browser's built-in reflected-XSS filter on every response and making the reflected/stored XSS vulnerabilities easier to exploit.

Content-Security-Policy is set to "default-src * 'unsafe-inline'", permitting scripts and content from any origin plus inline script, so the policy provides no XSS mitigation. No X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors directive is set anywhere, leaving the /danger account-deletion page frameable and clickjackable (CWE-1021).

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: Exception details are leaked to clients: on any handler error, content = str(ex) is returned via send_error(500, content), exposing internal exception messages (paths, SQL errors, etc.) in HTTP responses.

extra.message: Raw sqlite3.OperationalError exceptions from the injected query are returned to the attacker in the /users response, enabling error-based SQL injection and disclosing database internals.

extra.message: When --ssl is used, the TLS context is deliberately weakened: 'ctx.options &= ~ssl.OP_NO_SSLv3' re-enables the broken SSLv3 protocol (POODLE), and clearing OP_NO_COMPRESSION re-enables TLS compression (CRIME). These downgrade the confidentiality of encrypted connections.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: The TLS private key is loaded from './ssl/key.pem', a file committed to the repository (ssl/key.pem). Distributing a private key in source control compromises any deployment using it: anyone with repo access can impersonate the server or decrypt traffic.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: User credentials are stored in plaintext and committed to the repository in db/users.xml (e.g. admin password 'Y3RFgwZP$v6v#D' on line 7, plus weak passwords 'guest', 'babygirl', '123456' on lines 14, 21, 28). These values are loaded verbatim into the users table by dsvpwa/server.py, so the database stores cleartext passwords with no hashing.
